root.name: Owen Defense: Matovinsky Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 b6 2. d4 Bb7 3. Bd3 f5 4. exf5 Bxg2 5. Qh5+ g6

overview: Black replies to Bd3 with 3...f5, and after 4.exf5 Bxg2 5.Qh5+ g6 the position is chaotic with Black's bishop on g2 and the king exposed. White has an extra pawn or more and Black's counterplay is thin. It is a speculative line that is rarely good against accurate play.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawns and keep the extra material with Qh5+ and fxg6
Trade queens or hit Black's king while it is exposed

black_ideas.idea: Pick off the g2 pawn and open lines to the rook
Hold the bishop and create mating chances

typical_structures.structure: Open centre, Black kingside in ruins

character.notes: Both kings face tactics early and one error loses fast.

gambit.notes: White keeps the extra pawns if it avoids the traps.

soundness.notes: Bauer calls it suicidal; sound enough only against weak play.

structure.notes: All centre pawns are gone and files are open.

approach.notes: Almost never played by strong players.

level.notes: Specific forcing lines but unsound, so not a repertoire choice.

character.reason: Black's king is exposed and the play is tactical.

gambit.reason: Black offers pawns that White can keep.

soundness.reason: The parent source calls it suicidal.

structure.reason: Pawns are traded early and the position is open.

approach.reason: Strong players almost never choose this.

level.reason: It is dubious, so never Beginner.

plans.reason: Black hopes for development and counterplay against an exposed king.
